text:
lina: FYI customer (AcmeRetail) opened a ticket — they keep seeing unexpected KMS decrypt events tied to their Dedicated deployment. Asking for an immediate log pull and advice. They said it started ~10:15 UTC and included an example key path.
matt: ack. can you paste the ticket id and the example key path here? also need customer org id, dedicated pool id, and any suspicious IPs if they have them.
lina: ticket #C-48231. key path: projects/acme-rd/locations/global/keyRings/retail-keys/cryptoKeys/session. customer says decrypts by unknown principal, 10:12-10:22 UTC. no IPs from customer yet.
oncall-sre: I'll take this. triage steps I'll run now: 1) pull KMS audit events for that key (10:00-11:00 UTC) 2) pull dedicated host access logs and gateway logs 3) check recent RBAC/IAM changes in past 72h 4) isolate any principals and block if unauthorized.
dj: ran a quick query in internal-logsearch: found 8 decrypt operations on that key between 10:11-10:19 UTC. Sample log line:
```
{"timestamp":"2026-03-16T10:13:21Z","method":"Decrypt","resource":"projects/acme-rd/locations/global/keyRings/retail-keys/cryptoKeys/session","principal":"serviceAccount:redwood-dedicated-svc@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com","src_ip":"10.44.128.9","zone":"us-east1"}
```

dj: principal looks like our dedicated runtime service account. could be expected if customer is using platform-managed CMEK. need to confirm whether this customer configured CMEK or we are using platform key on their pool.
anya: important: preserve evidence. do NOT rotate the key yet until we have snapshot copies of logs and the customer's confirmation to proceed. also we should check whether there were any recent RBAC grant changes that could have given broader access to that service account.
matt: reaching out to customer now: "We're investigating urgently. Please confirm whether you've configured a customer-managed key (CMEK) for your Dedicated pool or if you're using Redwood-managed keys. Also send any app logs around 10:10-10:20 UTC and any IPs you consider suspicious. We'll update in 2 hours or sooner." :thumbsup:
lina: customer replied: they did not knowingly enable CMEK and believe they use platform key by default. they attached a container log snippet with a request to /v1/generate that correlates to 10:12.
oncall-sre: quick additional check: checked our key mapping service — this Dedicated pool is tied to platform-managed key id "redwood/dedicated/default-session-key". that maps to the service account seen in logs. outcome: decrypts are from our runtime, not external principal.
anya: ok that reduces exfil suspicion but still need root cause: why did the customer see it as unexpected. steps: 1) reconcile customer app requests with our decrypts 2) confirm we didn't recently grant extra IAM roles to third parties 3) verify KMS integration config surfaced in console 4) send post-incident summary and recommend config hardening (CMEK guidance) 5) add alert rule for unexpected cross-customer decrypts.
dj: noted. I found an IAM change event 2026-03-15T03:50Z where a tooling job updated service account bindings across pools to add "roles/logging.viewer" — looks non-sensitive but I'll cross-check diffs for anything that touched crypto keys or KMS IAM.
kms-bot: Automated alert: 6 decrypt operations detected on key projects/acme-rd/locations/global/keyRings/retail-keys/cryptoKeys/session from serviceAccount:redwood-dedicated-svc@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com between 10:11-10:19 UTC.
matt: customer asked if we can temporarily restrict access to the key while investigation continues. what's recommended?
anya: recommended: 1) create a deny binding for the key for non-essential service accounts (temporary) OR 2) if we can't deny at key granularity quickly, quiesce routing for that Dedicated pool (brief maintenance window) and inform customer. also offer to rotate the key once we have forensics copies.
oncall-sre: I've created a temporary IAM deny binding scoped to all non-platform service accounts on that key and restricted pool egress (applied at 10:40 UTC). captured signed log snapshots and exported to locked bucket for legal. notify customer that we applied a temporary restriction.
lina: customer acknowledged and asked for timeline and the exported logs. sent them a secure link to the log bundle and ETA 90 mins for deeper analysis.
dj: further analysis: decrypts correspond to normal session retrievals from the runtime dealing with cached sessions after a backend rollout at 09:58 UTC. rollout caused repeated session fetches which look anomalous in volume for that short window. not an unauthorized access.
anya: final action items: - confirm rollout caused spikes and add rate-limits to session decrypts - add per-customer KMS usage dashboard and a threshold alert (>5 decrypts/min outside normal window) - surface CMEK option to customers and doc how to lock keys to customer-managed KMS - add RBAC review in our Change Approval flow for any job that touches KMS IAM
matt: sending customer summary and closure: "We found the decrypts were from our runtime tied to a backend rollout, not an external compromise. We preserved logs, applied a temporary deny while we investigated, and recommend enabling CMEK or adding key-level controls. We'll follow up with concrete hardening steps and a postmortem." :white_check_mark:
anya: looping in legal/compliance for record-keeping and for any follow-up with the customer. marking this P2 and will track post-incident items in the security board.
oncall-sre: closing the incident thread here — will open a postmortem doc and link to ticket #C-48231 when ready.
